features.name: Sailing on the campaign map (land/sea switching, wind-and-navigation speed)
features.summary: Parties can leave the coast and move across open water on the world map. When a party enters a water face it becomes a fleet (ship icon, at-sea flag); its speed then depends on the Navigation skill, ship types, crew and the current wind ($beaufort). Reaching land near a port/jetty/landing point disembarks it again.
features.mechanics: Engine callback script:game_get_party_speed_multiplier (187 stmts, VC-new) reads party_get_current_terrain; terrain 0/7/8 (water) -> calls calculate_party_speed_water (navigation skill skl_navigation, crew/ship types, $beaufort wind) and, for AI parties, sets party slot 296=1 + party flag 512 and calls update_party_icon (ship icon). Back on land it clears slot 296/flag 512. For the player, sea travel is gated by slot 296: if the player is on water without being 'at sea' it snaps him to the nearest ferry/jetty (p_ferry_1a..p_jetty_1) or port town (party slot 241 = coastal) and sets $auto_enter_town, else get_next_land_position. Embark/disembark run switch_to_water_consequences / switch_to_land_consequences from menus (landet_ships_encounter, landing_point_encounter, port_encounter, ferry_encounter, player_lair_menus embark). It also clamps the player inside the map bounds. strig:136 (every 2.1h, only while slot 296=1) applies at-sea morale loss at night or with low Navigation and storm damage to ships.

skill: skl_navigation (repurposed skill: +5% sea speed per level)
map: VC map.txt with navigable sea faces

features.name: Owning a fleet: ship types, crew capacity, hull damage, buying/building/capturing ships
features.summary: The player owns up to 7 ships, each with a type (Busse, Skeid, Karvi, Snekkja, Knorr, Byrding and more), a name, a hull condition and build quality/material. Ship capacity limits how many troops you can carry to sea; storms can damage or sink ships and excess crew is lost. Ships are bought or built (choosing wood) from port chiefs, captured after sea battles and managed in a ship screen.
features.mechanics: Ships are a struct array on the party: slots 301-307 = ship type, 311-317 = name (pseudo-troop or string), 321-327 = hull condition, 331-337 = encoded modifiers (decoded by decode_value / encode_values_to_reg0). get_ship_properties(type) returns the stat table in reg1..reg7 (speed, ?, ?, price, hit points, crew capacity reg6, name string). cf_crew_fit_in_ships sums reg6 over slots 301-307 and fails if party size exceeds it (used by embark menus/dialogs). strig:136 rolls storm damage per ship by $beaufort, compacts the array when a ship sinks, and removes random non-hero troops that no longer fit. Port chief dialogs (port_chief_buy_ship, port_chief_build_ship_main_*) and prsnt_vc_submenu_ships / prsnt_vc_submenu_ships_customize sell/customise ships; menu_ship_capture adds an enemy ship after victory; give_ships_to_towns (trig:6) seeds port inventories; calculate_ship_value prices them; merge_ships_from_party_to_party / give_player_ships_from_party_to_party move ships between the player and landed-ship parties.

features.name: Ship-to-ship deck battles with boarding
features.summary: When the player's fleet meets an enemy at sea the fight happens on real ships on water: each side's ships are spawned as moving scene-prop hulls, agents ride on deck, ships sail, rock in the waves, collide, run aground and board each other. Weather (storm scenes, wind prop) and wave shaders are set per battle.

features.name: Paid passage between ports
features.summary: A port chief can sell the player passage to another port: the party is carried by a transporter ship and auto-enters the destination town on arrival. Marshals with a whole army are refused unless a big enough passenger ship is in port.

features.name: Formations v2 with on/off toggle and native-rank fallback
features.summary: VC ships a newer Motomataru 'complex formations' build: complex formations can be switched off in VC's options screen; when on, formation orders form true formations (ranks, shield wall, wedge, column); when off, the same orders fall back to Warband's native spacing orders. A first-use dialog explains the system.
features.mechanics: Keyboard entry: mst:lead_charge/t133 (game_key_clicked 26 = order key) reads $FormAI_off (written only by prsnt:vc_options/t2): when on it sets $gk_order=26, shows prsnt_order_display (when $controller_in_use=0) and a one-time dialog_box (str_formations, bit 1024 of $first_time); when off it prints 'Formations turned OFF'; t129 (F1 hold-timer, $when_f1_first_detected >=250 ms), t136 (key_f7) and t137 (key_f8) dispatch to the formation scripts. Each formation key calls player_order_extended_formations (if $FormAI_off=0 -> player_attempt_formation per listening division) or player_order_regular_formations (-> formation_to_native_order). formation_to_native_order issues team_give_order stand_closer (7) N times to reach the requested spacing; its rank orders (mordr_form_1..5_row = 22..26) sit behind an always-true (eq,0,0) branch and are therefore dead code in this build. pick_native_formation -> calculate_default_ranks picks a rank count from division size. Support: form_infantry (536), form_cavalry, form_archers, battlegroup_place_around_pos1, store_battlegroup_data (486), formation_end, agent_fix_division. Wired into lead_charge, village_attack_bandits, village_raid, quick_battle_battle and VC story battles.

features.name: Remembered per-division formations and placements across battles
features.summary: The player can save how each division should be formed and spaced; at the start of every later battle VC automatically re-applies those formations and spacing to each division and reports it ('Division N <class> formed ...').

features.name: Christian/pagan religion of settlements, slow conversion and player faith
features.summary: Every town, fort and village has an official religion (Christian or pagan) and a Christian-population percentage that drifts over time. Religious buildings, the lord's own faith and the nearest monastery or hof push it; when the minority grows past a threshold the settlement flips. The player picks a faith at character creation and can convert later; whether a settlement shares the holder's faith changes its relation with the player, and the player's minister reports kingdom-wide conversion progress. Faith also scales weekly fief income: strig:116 multiplies a player-owned center's rent by the share of people who share the player's faith.
features.mechanics: strig:103 (every 0.62h) picks one random center (p_town_1..p_salt_mine) that is not plundered (party slot 344=0): party slot 235 = Christian share 0-100 is nudged by religion buildings (improvement slots 134 Christian Monastery / 140 Christian Church, 136 Temple to Odin / 142 Shrine to Norse Gods), the holder lord's faith (troop slot 16: 1=Christian, 2=pagan) and the closest unplundered monastery (p_monasterio1..) or hof (p_paganholysites1..) within 20 map units, with log messages; improvement 145 (Merchants' Rest Hall) also adds prosperity (slot 50), 146 (Scriptorium) can raise the player's reading and 141 (Brewery) relation. For centers the player owns, slot 26 (relation) moves up or down depending on $g_player_faith vs slot 234 (official religion 1/2) and the share; slot 397 modifies it. Above 80% share a pagan center may flip slot 234 to Christian (and the mirror case). $faith_conversion accumulates when centers of the player's kingdom move toward the player's faith and is reported by the minister (dlga_minister_faith). menu_village_force_convert1 lets the player forcibly convert a village (5 hours; success from persuasion, power strike, attributes, character-creation virtue/defect, the share), and the center_manage options center_build_religion1-4 build churches/hofs. Faith is chosen in menu_start_game_2/4 ($religion_type -> $g_player_faith) and changed at monasteries/hofs (vc.monasteries_and_hofs). cf_troop_religion_matches_players gates recruitment and some dialogs.

features.name: Monasteries and pagan hofs as visitable map sites (donate, learn to read, convert, recruit, pillage)
features.summary: Monasteries and hofs are their own map locations. The player can visit the monks or the hof, donate 500 for a blessing, pay 4000 to learn to read, convert to that faith, recruit (monks/priests at monasteries, berserkers at hofs), or pillage the site for silver and goods - which leaves it ruined and smoking for weeks and stops it influencing local religion.

features.name: Siege planning: blockade, sanitation, treachery, sabotage, burning fields, starvation and siege equipment
features.summary: Besieging becomes a multi-day operation. From a siege-planning menu the player can build a blockade (circumvallation) that protects the camp and starves the town, dig latrines to avoid disease, send men to find a traitor inside, send infiltrators to burn food stores or poison wells, and burn the surrounding fields (results depend on harvest season). Defenders run out of food, may sally out or surrender starving, can be asked for tribute or hostages, and the assault needs ladders/mantlets brought up first.
features.mechanics: menu:castle_besiege offers siege_warfare_p -> menu:siege_plan, which summarises state into s15-s20 from party slot 400 (blockade 0/1 building/2 done), $g_traicion_interna (betrayal 1-4), $g_campos_cercanos (fields 1-3), $g_infiltracion_interna (infiltration 1-4), $g_siege_saneamiento (sanitation, timed off slot 403 hours) and offers build_circunvalation / close_circunvalation / build_varios / traicion_interna / infiltracion_interna / destruir_campos_a/b / town_investigar. Outcome menus: traicion_resultado1-5 / traicion_lucha, infiltracion_resultado1-5 (+_c variants), campos_cercanos1-4 (season-dependent food), construct_saneamiento, construct_circunvalation. prsnt_infiltrationandsabotage picks the sabotage target (writes slot 405). Starvation: $g_days_spent_starving / $g_next_sally_at / $g_sally_timer advanced in menu:castle_besiege -> menu_nofood_siege_defenders_sally or menu_surrender_siege_defenders_starved. Assault prep: menu:siege_assault with $g_listos_para_asalto, $g_mantlets_1, build_mantlet / build_ladders, menu_poner_escaleras(_mantlets); mst castle_attack_walls_belfry/t95 and _ladder/t69 read $g_mantlets_1. Negotiation dialogs player_siege_ask_surrender / player_hostage_surrender / player_siege_tributo read starvation state. lift_siege and castle_taken reset everything.

features.name: Plundering captured towns, loot choices, recovery time and slave-taking
features.summary: When a town or fort falls the player can sack it (a street-fighting plunder scene and a lump of silver, keeping or not keeping control), which leaves it 'plundered' for weeks with a changed map icon. Raided villagers can be hunted down as slaves, slave traders operate in towns (and can be banned), and after battle a loot-options menu decides how the spoils are split.

features.name: Lasting battle wounds on the player (head/face/body), healing and permanent scars
features.summary: A heavy blow in any battle can give the player a serious wound to a body location that temporarily costs attribute points. Each day the wound either heals (helped by Wound Treatment) or worsens toward a permanent scar; a wound report and character-screen section list healing wounds and scars, and barbers/physicians in larger towns can cure them for a fee. Can be turned off.
features.mechanics: Every SP battle template has a ti_on_agent_hit trigger (e.g. mst:lead_charge/t21, village_attack_bandits/t37, sea_battle/t45 - ~50 templates) that, when $vc_wounds_on=1, the victim is the player and damage >= 20 (scaled by options_get_damage_to_player), rolls 20% and a further check against existing wounds and character level, picks a location from the hit bone (head/face/body), removes attribute points and records them in qst_vc_wounds quest slots: 31-34 = per-location timer (positive = days until permanent, negative = healing), 41-44 = attribute points lost, 51-54 = scars; increments $wounded_today / $total_wounds_ever. strig:133 (every 23.8h) advances each timer using party Wound Treatment x5 %: healed wounds give the attributes back (troop_raise_attribute: slot 41->INT, 42->CHA, 43->STR, 44->AGI); expired ones become permanent scars; posts a Wound Report dialog. store_wound_report builds the text for prsnt_character_screen_main and battle_debrief. Barber dialogs (dlga_barber_cureh_*) test slots 31-34 and cure.
evidence: dis vc mst:lead_charge/t21:conseq (ti_on_agent_hit): $vc_wounds_on, damage>=20, 20% roll, quest slots 41-44, $total_wounds_ever

features.name: Battle immersion: war cries, horns, shield taunts, berserker rage and morale spreading from nearby events
features.summary: Morale in battle becomes local: kills, wounds and hits shake or steel the troops standing near them, with stronger effects close by. The player (and AI troops) can bellow a war cry, sound a horn or bang shields to raise nearby allies' courage, and the player can enter a timed berserker rage (more damage and speed, worse accuracy) with a cooldown and on-screen bar.
features.mechanics: change_courage_around_agent(amount, agent) adds amount x 50/40/30/20/10 to agent slot 16 (Native's courage score) of every same-side human within 20/40/70/110/160 m; called from ti_on_agent_killed_or_wounded (mst:lead_charge/t72) and ti_on_agent_hit (t29) triggers in ~56 templates, on top of a modified apply_effect_of_other_people_on_courage_scores (189 vs Native 186 stmts) and apply_death_effect_on_courage_scores. features.summary: Riders can be knocked off their horses by heavy hits, blunt blows hurt horses differently, AI infantry use shield bashes, and whether a downed man is killed or only wounded depends on what hit him (spears, axes and stones kill; clubs and sticks knock out).

features.name: Expanded fief buildings (church/temple, mead hall, brewery, scriptorium, guild hall, slave market, blacksmith)
features.summary: Fief owners get many more buildings than Native's six: Christian monastery or church, temple/shrine to the Norse gods, mead hall, brewery, merchants' rest hall, scriptorium, blacksmith and slave market, each with a price and an effect on religion, prosperity, relation, income or the player's learning.

features.name: Recruiting requires the local lord's permission, which can be revoked
features.summary: Players cannot freely recruit in other lords' towns and villages: they ask the lord for permission. If the lord's (or the village's) opinion of the player drops too low the permission is revoked with a message; ownership changes also reset it.
features.mechanics: Party slot 239 per center = permission state (0 none/allowed-by-default, 1 revoked/denied, 2/3 transient). dlga_reclutar_permiso1 (lord_talk) grants it; strig:161 (every 48h) resets transient states, and when $recruitment_on=0 revokes permission in towns whose lord's relation with the player is < -10 (50%), villages with center relation < -20, or lord relation < -25, printing '{lord} revokes your right to recruit'. give_center_to_lord clears it on new owners. prsnt_vc_submenu_recruits2 writes it from the recruit UI.

features.name: Prisoner revolts in over-stretched AI parties
features.summary: Lords, bandits, sea raiders and farmers who carry far more prisoners than guards risk a revolt: the prisoners break free and become a roaming deserter band (with a leader if large), so big prisoner trains don't stay locked up forever.
features.mechanics: strig:166 (every 36h) iterates all parties whose type is a lord party (party slot 0 = 13) or whose template is in the looters..kidnapped_girl, sea_raiders_ships..chimney_smoke or village_farmers ranges; if prisoners exceed fighting members by more than 4 (20 for ship raiders) all non-hero prisoner stacks are moved into one or two temp parties, spawned as pt_deserters near the party (sea raiders: near a random coastal point p_battle_stones..p_bjorn_camp), set to fac_deserters, patrol radius 40, and given trp_looter_leader2 if > 25 men. strig:169 (every 20h) then caps/splits oversize deserter parties (removes > 1000, thresholds 190/220/300).
evidence: dis vc strig:166: prisoners vs guards test, spawn_around_party pt_deserters, party_set_faction fac_deserters, leader if >25
dis vc strig:169: deserter size thresholds 190/220/300/1000

features.name: Player-built refuge (hideout) that grows into a fortified base
features.summary: Without owning a fief, the player can build a personal hidden refuge on the map: a base to rest, store troops, hold banquets, hire staff (captain, priest, bard, tavernkeeper, trainer, smith, armorer, barber, cook) and train recruits. The captain can expand it in stages and add jetties so ships can dock there; it can be demolished.
features.mechanics: menu_build_refuge_new -> make_lair: relocates p_yourlair near the player, give_center_to_lord(player), enable_party, $lair_on=1, slot 390=0 (construction stage) and resets ten staff globals. menu_player_lair_menus offers hall/mead hall scenes, banquet, rename (prsnt_set_playerlair_name), staff hiring (prsnt_lair_hire_staff), garrison, ships/embark (if slot 241 coastal), demolish (demoler_lairm). Lair captain dialogs (lair_captain_improve*, lair_captain_add_port_*) start upgrades: slot 390 1->2->3->4 timed by slot 399 + strig:113 (every 24h: stage 1->2 once 160 h have passed since slot 399; strig:114 is the parallel later-stage timer, not disassembled); add_jetty_system sets slot 297. Training: trainer staff + strig:121 cf_process_training_fail (up to tier-3 troops). Battles near the refuge use scn_player_hideout_1/3/5 by stage (simple_encounter attack branch).

features.name: AI sea traffic: traders, fishers, slavers, travellers and sea kings sailing between ports
features.summary: The seas are populated by AI ships - fishing boats, slave traders, passenger ships, walrus hunters and Norse sea-king fleets - that embark at ports, sail to destination ports and land; raiders can land at coastal landing points. Pools are refilled over time and parties stranded on land are cleaned up.
features.mechanics: trig:9 (every 10.2h) calls refill_sea_party_template (spawns pt_fisher_ship / pt_slave_trader_ship / pt_traveller_ship up to $pin_limit, marks party slot 296=1 at sea, slot 123 home) and refill_sea_king_partys (pt_sea_king_norweg / _danish). map_sea_ai_1 (strig:131, 33.3h) assigns destinations; map_sea_ai_2 (strig:132, 0.7h) moves embarked parties between ports, embarks/disembarks them (pt_landet_ships / pt_port) and handles player auto-travel; map_sea_ai_3 (strig:79, 3h) handles landed raiders/priest/pagan/routed parties. AI-party travel state lives in party slots 331-334 (target port, phase, timers) plus 297 (port link) and 73. remove_sea_parties_on_land (strig:131) deletes sea-only parties that end up ashore. Spawn points carry party slot 44 (sea zone 1/2) used by spawn_lairs / sea spawning.
evidence: sqlite calls: trig:9 -> refill_sea_party_template/refill_sea_king_partys; strig:131 -> map_sea_ai_1/remove_sea_parties_on_land; strig:132 -> map_sea_ai_2; strig:79 -> map_sea_ai_3

features.name: Defeated kingdoms can be reborn; their landless lords roam as 'adventurers'
features.summary: When a kingdom is destroyed its lords do not just vanish: they become adventurers who roam, sell prisoners and seek service, and may defect into other kingdoms. Over time, rumours of rebellion grow and a destroyed kingdom can rise again by retaking a walled center, with its old king and supporting lords rejoining (about one restoration a month late in the game).
features.mechanics: fac_adventurers (referenced in 39 blocks: party_get_ideal_size, calculate_troop_ai, npc_decision_checklist_party_ai, process_village_raids, spawn_bandits, strig:22/32/47/49...) is the holding faction for lords of defeated factions. strig:109 (every 0.05h) drives adventurer parties: wander near towns (patrol radius 35), sell prisoners via sell_prisoners, or hole up in their faction's center. strig:154 (every 30h): if the player's leadership + charisma/2 roll fails, picks a random defeated kingdom (faction slot 21 set, ruler troop without a party), counts its former lords now serving elsewhere and their fiefs, drops their relation with their current liege (-30) and posts '(Possible Rebellion) Rumors...' messages that escalate; on success the faction is restored (menu_notification_kingdom_reborn, change_troop_faction for leader + supporters). trig:51 (60h) handles center restoration (menu_notification_center_restoration, give_center_to_faction). Modified lord_find_alternative_faction / strig:49 run defections, now preferring culture and liege relation.
evidence: dis vc strig:154: leadership/charisma gate, defeated faction pick, lords of that faction elsewhere, -30 liege relation, 'Possible Rebellion' messages, menu_notification_kingdom_reborn
dis vc strig:109: fac_adventurers lord parties, sell_prisoners in towns, patrol behaviour

features.name: Marshal elections with candidates and lord votes
features.summary: Instead of the king silently picking a marshal, a faction periodically holds an election: two candidates are put forward, lords give their support, the player can be asked to stand as a candidate (accept or decline) and sees a screen with each candidate's supporters.
features.mechanics: strig:33 (every 24h) checks the player's faction and opens prsnt_marshal_selection (candidates #1/#2, 'Number of Supporters', 'Whom do you wish to support', '{s1} gives his support...'); globals $g_presentation_marshal_selection_max_renown_1/_2 (+_troop) hold the top-renown candidates. menu_marshal_selection_candidate_ask (accept / reject) when the player is suggested. The winner is installed by appoint_faction_marshal (a renamed copy of Native appoint_faction_marshall, 64 stmts: party_set_marshall, relation changes for disappointed lords, log entry 32).

features.name: Player ambitions ('Set goal') with tracked metrics and rewards
features.summary: The player chooses a life goal - raider, warrior, lord, king, expand the realm, or a custom target - and sets sliders for renown, wealth, army size, reputation, marriage etc. The game tracks progress, reports success as an event and grants a goal-specific reward.
features.mechanics: prsnt_set_goal (opened by button_open_set_goal_prsnt from the camp/character screens or menus) stores $goal_type and slider targets (goal_slider_values); prsnt_view_current_goal shows progress via view_goal_metric. trig:50 (every 25h) calls set_goal_check_success_event -> set_goal_check_metrics_progress, which tests cf_goal_renown_completed / cf_goal_wealth_completed / cf_goal_armysize_completed / cf_goal_reputation_completed / cf_goal_married_completed / cf_goal_rtr_completed / cf_goal_special_case_lord_king; on success set_goal_rewards: raider = +5 mountain bandits, warrior = +30 to all weapon proficiencies, lord/king/expand call set_goal_lord_reward / set_goal_king_reward / set_goal_expand_reward. update_savegame_to_content_update sets $set_goal_new_game_trigger for old saves.

features.name: On-load savegame repair and content-update migration
features.summary: Every time the game returns to the world map, VC runs a large maintenance trigger: it repairs known save corruptions (banners, item info, a v2.049 bug with a dedicated 'your save is ruined' menu) and, once per save, migrates old saves to a content update (new globals, parties, troops, items) so players don't need a new game.
features.mechanics: strig:165 has interval -75, which is the ti_on_switch_to_map event (not a periodic timer). Its 932 statements reset mission globals, re-run initialize_item_info, fix banners (give_troop_next_banner, 'fixing banners'), re-apply titles, food consumption, marshal checks, jump to menu_reconstruct_pre2049 when a known-corrupted state is detected, and finally - when neither $game_started_with_content_update nor $game_updated_to_content_update is 1 - call update_savegame_to_content_update (138 stmts: sets ~20 new globals, fixes p_ferry_4a/4b, jetties, tunics, ransom brokers, qst_vc_menu, prints 'Content update applied').
evidence: dis vc strig:165 header: interval -75.0 (= ti_on_switch_to_map); stmt 78 jump_to_menu menu_reconstruct_pre2049; stmts 928-930 content-update gate -> update_savegame_to_content_update
sqlite refs/globals update_savegame_to_content_update: writes savegame_id, goal_type, g_sgfix...; refs p_ferry_4a/4b, qst_vc_menu
Changelog 2.025 'reinitialize item info (wiped out in someone's save game by unknown cause)'

features.name: Seasons that change scene lighting/shaders and map time
features.summary: The year has seasons; every ten days a trigger advances the season, and every scene (towns, villages, battles) adjusts sun/ambient colours and season shader for spring, summer, autumn or winter. Season also feeds gameplay text such as harvest-time results when burning fields during a siege.
features.mechanics: strig:138 (every 240.1h) advances $shader_season (also set at game_start; cheat menu option 'season'; menu_season_change). calculate_season_light (30 stmts, reads only $shader_season) is called from 85 mission templates' load triggers (town_default/t7, town_center/t9, lead_charge/t66...) and adjusts scene lighting per season. Siege menus campos_cercanos1-4 branch on harvest season. MP equivalent: scene_init_weather_and_sounds (MP templates only).
evidence: sqlite globals shader_season: 102 reads, writers game_start, strig:138, z_code_season, cheat option
sqlite calls: calculate_season_light called from 85 templates

features.name: Camp, character, faction and troop-tree report screens
features.summary: A presentation-based camp menu replaces many Native report menus: tabbed screens for the character (bio, wounds, honour, goal), followers/companions (morale, opinions), kingdom (lords, relations, armies, economy, centres, diplomacy, orders), ships, a full troop upgrade tree, and a troop detail screen that shows a troop's equipment and stats on a 3D model.
features.mechanics: menu:camp opens prsnt_camp_screen_main (also _siege and _sea variants); tabs build text via ~30 texto_* scripts (texto_kingdomlords_info 154, texto_lords_relation 153, texto_partysize_morale 163, texto_kingdom_economy 100, texto_kingdom_armies 59, texto_companions_report 246, texto_global_camp_info 128...). prsnt_character_screen_main (engine-hooked via game_character_screen_requested) and prsnt_faction_screen_main. prsnt_troop_tree / prsnt_game_troop_tree draw upgrade trees with troop_tree_precurse/recurse; prsnt_troop_detail uses troop_detail_* (layout, stats, inventory, tooltips, dummy agent tableaux) to inspect any troop. prsnt_show_companions + companions_camp_conversation for companion talk.

features.name: Civilian second outfit worn automatically in towns and halls
features.summary: The player keeps a second (civilian) outfit that is worn automatically when walking around towns, courts and certain quest scenes, instead of full battle gear; its shield still counts for skill modifiers.

features.name: Weekly trade ledger in the budget report and anti-exploit price formulas
features.summary: Everything the player buys or sells is tallied for the week, split into trade goods and other items, and shown as its own lines in the weekly budget report. The buy/sell price formulas were also reworked so that buying and selling the same item repeatedly no longer makes money.
features.mechanics: Modified engine-called game_event_buy_item / game_event_sell_item (58 vs Native 23 stmts) price the transaction via game_get_item_buy_price_factor / game_get_item_sell_price_factor (57/89 vs Native 18/20) and accumulate $num_buyed_goods_in_week / $buyed_goods_in_week_for (trade goods itm_mead..itm_siege_supply) or $num_buyed_items_in_week / $buyed_items_in_week_for (other items), with the mirror $num_selled_* / $selled_* on sales. They still push the town's trade-good price slot (party slot 251 + good index) up by 14 (buy) or 21 (buy-back), capped at 10000. prsnt:budget_report/t0 reads and resets the ledger weekly.
evidence: dis vc game_event_buy_item: price factor, goods/items split into $num_buyed_*/$buyed_*_in_week_for, price slot 251+good +14/+21
